title: Rollouts: block canary progression when error budget is exhausted (tier/service scoped) + audit logging
author: Jada Williams
description: Context: As part of the tiered SLO + error budget enforcement work, we want teams to “feel” budget burn during progressive delivery instead of only after incidents. This PR wires error budget status into the canary rollout controller so that rollouts cannot automatically progress to the next stage when the relevant error budget is exhausted (scoped by tier + service, and optionally route group). What this does: (1) Adds a budget status lookup step in the canary progression loop that queries the control plane budget-check API and evaluates the result against the rollout’s tier/service scope. (2) Introduces a feature flag to control enforcement: rollouts.errorBudgetGating with modes off | warn_only | block (default: warn_only in prod after deploy; block enabled per-service in the pilot). (3) Blocks only forward progression (e.g., 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%); rollback/abort actions remain allowed even when budget is exhausted. (4) Adds structured audit logging for gating decisions and overrides (who/when/why/TTL), and surfaces the gating decision in the rollout event stream so Console can render “blocked due to error budget” with a link to the SLO dashboard. (5) Adds an override mechanism: an override token (minted by the existing admin endpoint) can be attached to a rollout to bypass blocking for a limited TTL; all uses are logged with reason and linked work item. Scope details: The budget scope key is (tier, owning_service, slo_group) where slo_group maps to the rollout target (gateway/chat, embeddings, catalog, etc.). For Dedicated tier, the key remains tier-scoped and does not include customer identifiers; customer-specific dedicated budgets will be addressed separately (this PR only consumes the scoped keys we already compute). Safety/behavior: - If the budget service is unavailable or returns unknown, we do not hard-block; we degrade to warn-only and emit an event + metric so oncall can fix the gating dependency without deadlocking deploys. - Block mode is only respected when (a) the feature flag is set to block for the rollout’s service, and (b) budget status == exhausted for the relevant window. - The decision is cached per rollout step for 60s to avoid hammering the budget endpoint during high-frequency reconcilers. Observability: Adds metrics rollouts_budget_gate_checks_total{service,tier,result} and rollouts_budget_gate_blocks_total{service,tier,reason}. Also adds log fields gate.result, gate.budget_window, gate.budget_remaining, gate.override_id. Testing: Unit tests for policy evaluation and caching; integration test harness with a fake budget-check server; e2e canary test covering off/warn_only/block and override TTL expiry. Rollout plan: ship with warn_only everywhere, then enable block for API gateway + routing services as part of the ENG-2427 pilot; publish runbook link and “how to override” doc in the rollout UI help panel. Follow-ups: (a) Console wiring to render the new gate events (DES-145), (b) tighten dedicated mappings once dedicated readiness SLI is in place, (c) revisit “unknown budget status” behavior after we have SLO job reliability numbers.

review_conversation: Paula Mendes: Can we confirm this only blocks forward progression and never prevents rollback/abort? Also please add an explicit note in the PR body and a test that abort is allowed under exhausted budget.
Jada Williams: Yep—blocking is only applied to the “advance stage” action; abort/rollback bypass gating. Added a test case and updated description.

Rafael Mendes: Concern about deadlock if budget-check dependency is down. I’d rather we fail open (warn-only) than block deploys due to our own reliability issues. Can we also emit a metric for unknown so we can alert on it?
Jada Williams: Agreed. Implemented fail-open to warn-only on unknown/error + added rollouts_budget_gate_checks_total{result=unknown} and a log line with gate.error_code.
Ethan Park: Please align timeout/retry behavior with the control plane client standard (250ms timeout, 2 retries with jitter). Also: cache results briefly to avoid QPS spikes from reconcilers.
Jada Williams: Updated client defaults to match standard + 60s cache per rollout step.

Connor O'Brien: Override path needs an audit trail including actor, reason, and TTL, and should require a linked work item (ENG/INC). Also ensure override tokens don’t get persisted into long-lived rollout templates accidentally.
Jada Williams: Added validation requiring reason + linked_key; overrides are stored only on rollout instance metadata (not template) and expire by TTL; audit records added.
Jordan Lee: Scope mapping: please document what happens when tier/service can’t be resolved from rollout target, and ensure we don’t silently map Dedicated -> Hosted.
Jada Williams: Added explicit validation; unresolved scope results in warn-only + event, and tier mismatches are rejected at config load time.
Marissa Cole: Can we surface a stable string code for Console to render (e.g., BUDGET_EXHAUSTED vs UNKNOWN)? We don’t want UI to parse freeform messages.
Jada Williams: Added gate.reason_code enum to the event payload + details string for humans.
release_notes: Rollout controller now consults error budget status and can block canary progression when budgets are exhausted (feature-flagged).
Adds audit logging and event stream fields to support Console messaging and override tracking.
